## Goals

-   Fit and interpret random-slope models
-   Distinguish nested and crossed random effects
-   Report population-level marginal effects from mixed models

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(marginaleffects)
```
:::



## Random slopes: sleep deprivation

`sleepstudy` (from `lme4`): reaction time of 18 subjects restricted to 3 hours of sleep per night over 10 days.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(sleepstudy, aes(Days, Reaction, group = Subject)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Reaction time over days of sleep restriction, by subject](week13-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-sleep-1.png){#fig-sleep width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_int <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
m_slope <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 + Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
anova(m_int, m_slope)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Data: sleepstudy
Models:
m_int: Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)
m_slope: Reaction ~ Days + (1 + Days | Subject)
        npar    AIC    BIC  logLik deviance  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
m_int      4 1802.1 1814.8 -897.04   1794.1                         
m_slope    6 1763.9 1783.1 -875.97   1751.9 42.139  2  7.072e-10 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(m_slope)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
lmerModLmerTest]
Formula: Reaction ~ Days + (1 + Days | Subject)
   Data: sleepstudy

REML criterion at convergence: 1743.6

Scaled residuals: 
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-3.9536 -0.4634  0.0231  0.4634  5.1793 

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev. Corr
 Subject  (Intercept) 612.10   24.741       
          Days         35.07    5.922   0.07
 Residual             654.94   25.592       
Number of obs: 180, groups:  Subject, 18

Fixed effects:
            Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  251.405      6.825  17.000  36.838  < 2e-16 ***
Days          10.467      1.546  17.000   6.771 3.26e-06 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Correlation of Fixed Effects:
     (Intr)
Days -0.138
```


:::
:::



How much does each subject's slope vary around the average?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
VarCorr(m_slope)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 Groups   Name        Std.Dev. Corr 
 Subject  (Intercept) 24.7407       
          Days         5.9221  0.066
 Residual             25.5918       
```


:::
:::



The population-average effect, with honest uncertainty:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_slope, variables = "Days")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 Term Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 Days     10.5       1.55 6.77   <0.001 36.2  7.44   13.5

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Compare with the random-intercept-only model:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_int, variables = "Days")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 Term Estimate Std. Error  z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 Days     10.5      0.804 13   <0.001 126.2  8.89     12

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



The estimate is the same, but the standard error grows when the model allows slopes to vary.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
predictions(m_slope, newdata = datagrid(Days = c(0, 9)), re.form = NA)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 Days Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 % Subject
    0      251       6.82 36.8   <0.001 984.4   238    265     308
    9      346      14.63 23.6   <0.001 407.5   317    374     308

Columns: rowid, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, Reaction, Subject, Days 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(m_slope, condition = "Days", re.form = NA) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Population-level prediction from the random-slope model](week13-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-slope-pred-1.png){#fig-slope-pred width=672}
:::
:::

## Exercise 1

Why is the standard error of the `Days` slope bigger with random slopes? What does that say about the effective sample size?
:::

## Nested random effects

`Pastes` (from `lme4`): strength of paste from 10 batches, each with 3 casks, each sampled twice.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_nest <- lmer(strength ~ 1 + (1 | batch/cask), data = Pastes)
VarCorr(m_nest)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 Groups     Name        Std.Dev.
 cask:batch (Intercept) 2.90408 
 batch      (Intercept) 1.28737 
 Residual               0.82341 
```


:::
:::



Which level has the most variability?

## Crossed random effects

`Penicillin`: inhibition zone diameter for 24 samples, each tested on all 6 plates (fully crossed).



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_cross <- lmer(diameter ~ 1 + (1 | plate) + (1 | sample), data = Penicillin)
VarCorr(m_cross)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 Groups   Name        Std.Dev.
 plate    (Intercept) 0.84670 
 sample   (Intercept) 1.93161 
 Residual             0.54992 
```


:::
:::
